title: Release exact owned native runtime resources after terminal, cancellation and consumer close
user_story: Long-running research agents must not leak proxy containers or destroy another invocation when a CLI turn ends.

requirements.description: Parent and wrapper share a fresh per-invocation owner; cleanup targets only its exact label and IPC volume.
Terminal completion and consumer close release owned resources even when the wrapper is stopped before its finally block.
Cleanup failure cannot become a successful request; resource count and command timeouts bound cleanup.
Controlled Python protocol fixtures identify their own executable and cannot reuse an unavailable vendor CLI health cache.

nonfunctional: Preserve existing API/SSE contracts, raw scientific evidence, user data, worktrees and every skills/agent file.
No new Research Engine, autonomy-level workflow stack, paid API fallback or protection bypass.
Mandatory software regression100% executed/PASS; desired100%coverage informational.
Live subscription inference, software fixture execution and scientific qualification remain separate evidence modes.
inputs: Existing authorized project-owned native CLI invocation
outputs: Owned runtime resources released or explicit cleanup error
preconditions: Reviewed installed-before-plan skills and owner architecture definition
postconditions: No new container/IPC-volume leak on actual checked invocation
No simulated transport is classified as actual Docker proof
dependencies: Authorized official native CLI and isolated runtime for actual provider checks
acceptance_criteria: Behavioral RED/GREEN and complete affected software regression
Actual Docker inspection and native smoke with no new owned runtime resources
Fresh full software gate before guarded dev push; independent exact-HEAD CI required

scenarios.expected: native launch shares a fresh owner with the runtime wrapper
docker cleanup uses exact owned label and volume only
invalid owner cannot start docker operations
completed turn releases owned runtime before reporting completion
consumer close releases its runtime without touching other requests
cleanup failure cannot be reported as a successful request
remaining owned resource is a cleanup failure
unexpected resource count is bounded and never bulk deleted
Real absent-vendor health remains UNAVAILABLE while independent Python protocol fixture completes and releases owned resources.

recovery: Preserve original failures and all attempts. Bounded development repair, exact request cancellation, no retries that hide failures. Missing live/research/UAT remains BLOCKED.
test_environment: MOCKED model/transport with real disposable backend state, actual controlled Python protocol processes and async boundaries; not scientific or remote CI proof.

review.method: Same-agent source and adversarial behavior review; independent acceptance/scientific review remains pending.

limitations: Protocol-process assertions use mocked Docker transport; worker REAL_LOCAL on original RED describes local processes, not live Docker/provider qualification.
Actual Docker inspection confirmed three proxy leaks after successful 6.5.8 native probes; initial smoke assertions did not cover cleanup.
First targeted green attempt exposed fixture-owned connector error state leaking into other cases; cleanup added without weakening assertions; raw failed report retained.
Actual corrected native probe proved no newly leaked container/volume relative to its captured baseline, not arbitrary host-crash recovery or all concurrent startup races.
Full capability learning and required exploratory AI-UAT adapters remain unqualified.
